data.name: LanguageHint
data.value: A new language applies when CashGear Capture starts again. In Arabic, windows are laid out right to left.

data.name: RestartForLanguage
data.value: Restart CashGear Capture now to show it in the new language?

data.name: SettingsSection
data.comment: Settings > General: the section with import, export and reset

data.name: SettingsTransferHint
data.value: Export saves the settings and the image editor's presets in one file, to keep a copy or use them on another PC. Passwords and tokens are never in it: destinations that need one ask for it again.

data.name: PortableFolder
data.value: This is a portable copy: its settings, logs and data are kept in {0}.

data.name: SettingsFileFilter
data.comment: File dialog filter: translate only the descriptions

data.name: SettingsFileName
data.comment: Suggested file name for an export

data.name: ConfirmImport
data.value: Replace all settings with the ones in {0}? The current settings are kept in a backup next to settings.json, and changes not applied yet in this window are lost.

data.name: ConfirmResetAll
data.value: Reset every setting to how it was when CashGear Capture was installed? The language and the choice about crash reports stay; the current settings are kept in a backup next to settings.json. Presets, history and recordings aren't touched.

data.name: ResetDone
data.value: Every setting is back to its default.

data.name: StepMissingTip
data.value: Its destination was deleted on the Destinations tab; the step is skipped.

data.name: AfterCaptureHint
data.value: Steps after "Open in the editor" wait for its Continue button, so they get the edited image. Servers, uploads, Word and the rest are set up on the Destinations tab.

data.name: AfterRecordingHint
data.value: A recording is always saved to the folder below first; these steps then send it on.

data.name: WaitForWindowsToHide
data.value: Wait for app windows to hide

data.name: CaptureDelayHint
data.value: The capture delay gives you time to open a menu or hover a tooltip before the screen is taken.

data.name: DelayPerKindHint
data.value: Repeat Last Capture waits as long as the kind of capture it repeats. An open menu is captured 3 seconds after you ask, unless set otherwise: time to open it.

data.name: IncludeWindowShadow
data.value: Add a drop shadow to window captures

data.name: ShowToolbarAtStartup
data.value: Show the capture toolbar when the app starts

data.name: CaptureToolbarHint
data.value: A small bar with a button for every kind of capture, always on top and never in a capture. Tray › Capture Toolbar shows it now; drag it by its grip, and drop it at the edge of a screen to dock it there.

data.name: ShapesHint
data.value: Any size can be typed (width × height). On the screen, Tab switches between the sizes and the mouse wheel changes the corner radius; the last ones used are kept. Freehand, polygon, rounded and menu captures are transparent outside their shape, so they are saved as PNG whatever the format on the Output tab.

data.name: ScrollingHint
data.value: Pick a window, then click where it scrolls. It is scrolled from where it is down to the bottom; Esc cancels. Allow more time for pages that load as they scroll.

data.name: CaptureMethodHint
data.value: Automatic avoids the yellow capture border on Windows 10 and still captures covered windows correctly.

data.name: CheckAgainTip
data.value: Test every encoder again (after a driver update or a new graphics card)

data.name: EncoderHint
data.value: Automatic uses the graphics card's encoder when it works here, which leaves the CPU free; otherwise the encoder built into Windows. If an encoder stops working during a recording, another takes over and the rest is saved as a second file.

data.name: MouseHint
data.value: Clicks, pointer effects, keystrokes and the webcam are on the Overlays tab.

data.name: RefreshAppsTip
data.value: List the apps running now (start the app first if it isn't listed)

data.name: NoiseSuppression
data.value: Noise suppression (RNNoise): remove fans, hum and typing, strength

data.name: NoiseGate
data.value: Noise gate: silence the microphone between words, below

data.name: Compressor
data.value: Compressor: even out loud and quiet speech

data.name: Limiter
data.value: Limiter: never let the microphone go above −1 dB (no clipping)

data.name: ProcessingHint
data.value: Applied to the microphone as it is recorded, in this order. The gate threshold is a peak level: set it between the room's noise and your quietest word. The microphone is held back 2 ms (10 ms more with noise suppression), and the recording takes that out, so it stays in sync.

data.name: LevelsHint
data.value: The meters listen while this page is open, to what a recording would record with the choices above. Speech peaking around −12 dB is right; the mark at the right end turns red when the sound clipped.

data.name: NormalizeLoudness
data.value: Even out the loudness to −16 LUFS when a recording is saved

data.name: LoudnessHint
data.value: Every recording then plays at the same loudness, the usual level for speech online, however loud the microphone or the sound was. Each sound track is measured, then encoded again (EBU R128, FFmpeg's loudnorm in two passes); the video is copied as it is. Peaks are kept below −1.5 dB. A silent track is left alone. Saving takes a few seconds more per 10 minutes.

data.name: AppAudioHint
data.value: Only one app records that app's sound (and that of the programs it starts) on whichever device it plays, and nothing else: no notifications, no other apps. All sound except one app leaves out, say, a call or music you don't want in the video. The app is found by its program when the recording starts, and followed if it starts or restarts later.

data.name: TracksHint
data.value: Sound is saved in the MP4 as AAC. Players play the first track only, so a track per source is for video editors. Volume and mute for each source are on the recording toolbar. Pause pauses the sound too. Without a sound device the video is recorded without sound, and the notification says so.

data.name: RecordingHint
data.value: Start and stop a recording from the tray or with the recording hotkey. Recordings are saved as MP4 in the capture folder. While recording, the video is written to a temporary file, so if the app or the PC stops, the recording can be saved from the tray menu afterwards.

data.name: HotkeysHint
data.value: Click a box and press the keys. Backspace clears it. Hotkeys are paused while a box is selected, so PrintScreen can be recorded.

data.name: PushToTalkHint
data.value: With a key set, the microphone is silent in recordings except while the key is held (and a quarter of a second after, so words aren't cut). The key isn't taken from other apps, so a key that does nothing in them works best: F13 to F24, Scroll Lock, Pause, or a mouse button mapped to one of those. A key on its own is fine here.

data.name: StartWithWindows
data.value: Start CashGear Capture when I sign in to Windows

data.name: OcrHint
data.value: Automatic reads the area with each of your Windows languages and takes every line from the language that matches its script, so Arabic and English in one area both work. More languages: Windows Settings › Time & language › Language › (language) › Options › Optical character recognition.

data.name: ScreenToolsHint
data.value: Inches and centimetres on the ruler follow Windows' scale of the monitor it is on. To measure real inches on the glass, set your screen's pixels per inch (its width in pixels divided by its width in inches). Tools are in tray › Tools and on the capture toolbar; set hotkeys for them on the Hotkeys tab.

data.name: HistoryHint
data.value: Recent captures are kept (with thumbnails) for tray › Recent Captures and Capture History, even ones you didn't save. Lowering the number removes the oldest straight away.

data.name: CheckForUpdates
data.value: Check for updates automatically (once a day) and download them in the background

data.name: OpenSettingsFileHint
data.value: Edits saved in the file apply immediately.

data.name: DiagnosticsHint
data.value: Saves a zip for a bug report: the last week's logs, the settings without server addresses, user names or passwords, and facts about this PC (Windows, graphics cards, monitors, sound devices). Nothing is sent anywhere.

data.name: FfmpegBuiltIn
data.value: FFmpeg {0}, built into the app (LGPL; see THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt).

data.name: DefaultOutputIs
data.value: The default output device is {0} now. If another becomes the default during a recording, system audio follows it; a device that is unplugged is recorded again when it is back.

data.name: NoOutputDevice
data.value: No sound output device was found; system audio is silent until one is connected.

data.name: EncoderAutomatic
data.value: Automatic: the best that works here (recommended)

data.name: CheckingEncoders
data.value: Checking which encoders work on this PC…

data.name: NoEncoderWorks
data.value: No encoder works on this PC, so recording is unavailable.

data.name: PushToTalkNotSet
data.value: Not set: the microphone is always recorded

data.name: PushToTalkInvalidError
data.value: Push to talk: "{0}" is not a valid key.

data.name: PushToTalkClash
data.value: Push to talk: {0} is already the hotkey for {1}.

data.name: MicTestIntro
data.value: Records 5 seconds of the microphone, then plays them back as recorded or as processed.

data.name: MicTestRecording
data.value: Recording 5 seconds: say something, and let the room be heard too…

data.name: MicTestRecorded
data.value: Recorded. Play it as recorded, or with the processing above; change the processing and play again to compare.

data.name: MicTestPlayed
data.value: Played. Play again, or record a new test.

data.name: HdrNoMonitor
data.value: No monitor is in HDR mode now.

data.name: HdrMonitor
data.value: {0} is in HDR mode (SDR content at {1:0} nits)

data.name: HdrExplanation
data.value: {0} On a monitor in HDR mode, captures, recordings and the magnifier read the screen in 16-bit float and turn it into SDR the way an SDR monitor would show it; HDR highlights brighter than SDR white become white. This uses Windows.Graphics.Capture, so Windows 10 shows its yellow border on that monitor.

data.name: OutputDeviceNotConnected
data.value: The output device chosen before (not connected)

data.name: FolderError
data.value: Folder: use a full path such as D:\Screenshots (or leave it empty for the default).

data.name: FixedSizeError
data.value: Fixed-size region: write the size as width × height in pixels, e.g. 800 × 600.

data.name: WorkflowEmptyError
data.value: After capture: switch on at least one step, such as "Open in the editor" or "Save to file".

data.name: AppNotChosenError
data.value: Sound: choose the app whose sound is recorded (or left out), or record all sound.

data.name: HotkeyNeedsModifier
data.value: Add Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win

data.name: HotkeyAloneError
data.value: {0}: {1} on its own would block that key in every app; add Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win.

data.name: TracksBoth
data.value: The mix, then one track per source

data.name: HdrAuto
data.value: Tone-map to SDR, as on the screen (recommended)

data.name: HdrOff
data.value: As Windows gives it to older apps (8-bit)
